## Luxury Brazil in 11 days: Rio, Iguazu and Buzios

The Luxury Brazil itinerary combines three kinds of holiday: city views and cultural life in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), Iguazu Falls on both sides of the border, and free days on the beaches of [Buzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). It lasts **11 days and 10 nights** and is operated as a private tour.

The main advantage is the individual organization of transfers and excursions, with options to add activities that match travelers' interests. But the word "luxury" does not mean that every premium service is already included: helicopter flights, VIP access, restaurant experiences and other options must be distinguished according to the actual terms of the program.

## How the journey is organized

| Stage | What awaits you |
|---|---|
| Rio | Panoramas, city life and free time |
| Iguazu | Both sides of the waterfalls |
| Buzios | Beaches and the ocean |

The journey starts in Rio with its classic sights. It then continues to Iguazu Falls. The last part takes place on the coast in Buzios, where there is time to relax without a packed sightseeing schedule.

Angra dos Reis and Ilha Grande are also mentioned as potential additional trips from Rio. Their appearance in the program does not make them guaranteed main overnight stops: the choice of such outings depends on the specific package and available time.

## Rio: Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and a private city guide

Rio is known for its granite hills, Atlantic coast and long urban beaches. Sightseeing focuses on Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the historic center. A Russian-speaking guide helps connect the panoramas with the city's history and explains the differences between seaside neighborhoods and older districts.

Options for a free day include the Botanical Garden, a helicopter ride over the city, culinary activities or an island excursion. These are ways of extending the tour, not a list of services all included simultaneously.

VIP access to Sugarloaf Mountain and Fast Track Gold are also optional enhancements. The cost, exact itinerary and availability of each are confirmed separately when booking.

## Iguazu: two countries in one journey

The main program covers both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu Falls. Around [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), travelers see broad panoramas of the waterfall system; on the Argentine side, reached via [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), the paths bring visitors closer to individual cascades.

That is why **Brazil and Argentina are listed as the two main countries**, despite the tour's name. The Argentine section focuses on the waterfalls, rather than a separate multi-day journey to Buenos Aires.

Planning needs to account for the border crossing, trail accessibility, transfer time and weather. Individual waterfall activities may be subject to their own restrictions.

## Buzios: a relaxed finale beside the ocean

After the busy city and nature excursions, the program continues to [Buzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). The resort peninsula is known for beaches, coves and pedestrian-friendly streets. Here, travelers can alternate time by the sea with boat trips.

This stage suits guests who want a quieter end to their journey. When selecting a hotel, it helps to decide whether proximity to a particular beach, walks around the center or seclusion matter most.

For another coastal destination, see [Angra dos Reis](/brazil/place/angra-dos-reis/), with its islands and boat excursions. A visit there remains optional unless a separate outing is included in the agreed itinerary.

## What is included and what costs extra

The price includes **hotel accommodation, excursions with Russian-speaking guides, guided transfers and driver-only transfers to Buzios**. High-class vehicles are specified for the main part of the journey, except around Iguazu Falls.

International flights, additional excursions and the domestic **Rio – Iguazu – Rio** flights are charged separately. The indicated expense for those flights starts at $700 per person NET, without commission. Meals and drinks during transfers are also excluded.

The 2027 program's starting price is **from $4609**. The final amount depends on dates, hotel categories and the services selected. To compare private tours, consider both the base price and the separate costs of flights and optional activities.

## Who will enjoy a private tour

This journey suits couples and small groups who appreciate personal assistance, the flexibility to select optional excursions and a relatively relaxed beach stay. It combines a city, natural landscapes and the sea without requiring travelers to organize all transfers themselves.

For other combinations of countries and cultural stops, see the [multi-country catalog](/multi-country/). The [Beach Holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/) section also helps select a tour by interest.

## Frequently asked questions about Luxury Brazil

### Why is this a multi-country tour?

Because the itinerary includes both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu Falls. The other main stages take place in Brazil.

### Is the flight to Iguazu included?

No. Domestic Rio – Iguazu – Rio flights are paid separately; the current description gives a starting estimate of $700 per person.

### Are all VIP services already included?

No. Helicopter rides, Fast Track Gold, VIP access and certain restaurant options are ways to extend the itinerary. Their inclusion and prices are agreed separately.

### Can I have more free time at the beach?

Private travel allows individual requests to be discussed. Any changes to duration and overnight stays need to be agreed before booking: the published base program lasts 11 days.

## Luxury Patagonia: a 10-day VIP tour of Argentina and Chile

The [private Luxury Patagonia VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/luxury-patagonia-10-days/) lasts **10 days and 9 nights**. It begins in Buenos Aires, travels through [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), Chile's [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) and Punta Arenas, and concludes in Santiago de Chile and the Maipo wine valley.

The route is designed for travelers who prefer private transfers, carefully organized accommodation and outstanding natural sights without strenuous multi-day trekking as the central goal. The program includes a glacier, a national park, the Strait of Magellan and two important South American cities.

## Ten days: destinations and sequence

| Days | Where the tour goes |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Buenos Aires, the city and tango |
| 3–4 | El Calafate and Perito Moreno |
| 5–6 | Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine |
| 7–8 | Punta Arenas, islands of the Strait of Magellan |
| 9–10 | Santiago and the Maipo Valley, departure |

The tour includes two main countries, Argentina and Chile. A border crossing and domestic flights connect different parts of Patagonia, where distances are great and weather conditions can vary considerably.

## Buenos Aires: Alvear Palace, a city tour and tango

On arrival in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a private transfer takes you to **Alvear Palace**. Day one is free for walks around Recoleta, San Telmo or Palermo.

Day two features a private city tour lasting about four hours. It covers La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada, the Obelisk, Recoleta and other neighborhoods. In the evening, a tango show makes Argentine music and dance an experience in its own right.

A Russian-speaking guide in Buenos Aires is included. This is convenient for travelers who want a cultural introduction before continuing through the natural parks.

## El Calafate: Perito Moreno's viewing walkways

The group travels to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) on day three. The following day is dedicated to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/). The ice field, Lake Argentino and viewing trails form one of the most famous natural areas of Argentine Patagonia.

Simply watching the glacier is a highlight: a wall of ice with blue cracks, the creaking of ice and shifting colors of the water. Large sections may break away, but the timing is impossible to predict.

A **Russian-speaking interpreter** is provided in El Calafate, unlike in Puerto Natales and Punta Arenas, where excursions are led by an English-speaking guide.

## Chilean Patagonia: Torres del Paine

On day five, you travel to [Puerto Natales](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). Day six takes you from there into [Torres del Paine National Park](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), famous for lakes of different colors, glacial valleys and granite towers.

This is not the same as a multi-day W or O trekking circuit. The package includes a park excursion, but longer athletic hikes should not be considered included without separate confirmation. For a scenic introduction to Chilean Patagonia, it is a way to experience the main landscapes before continuing to the Strait of Magellan.

## Punta Arenas and the Strait of Magellan islands

Day seven includes a transfer to [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/). On day eight, a boat excursion visits Magdalena and Marta islands, known for seabirds and wildlife in the Strait of Magellan. Weather has a particularly strong influence here on landing opportunities and boat schedules.

This is **an exception to the tour's predominantly private format**: the boat trip to the islands is not automatically a private excursion. Other transfers are arranged individually.

The program then includes a flight to Santiago de Chile.

## Santiago and the Maipo Valley: the finale

In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the itinerary includes a city tour and a visit to the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/), one of Chile's wine regions. After the glaciers and winds of Patagonia, the focus shifts to architecture, history and Chilean winemaking.

The final day ends with departure. This arrangement allows the journey to finish at a major air travel hub instead of retracing the whole route across Patagonia to the original city.

## What the price includes

Included services cover hotel accommodation with breakfast, private excursions except for the island boat trip, the specified guides, private transfers and national park admission tickets.

**Tour prices start at $8520.** International and domestic air tickets are listed as separate expenses. Optional excursions, food and drinks during transfers are not included either. When comparing VIP programs, remember to consider flight costs and included guiding services alongside hotel standards and the base price.

## VIP Patagonia or a longer trekking itinerary?

The ten-day tour suits those who want to see Perito Moreno, Torres del Paine and the Strait of Magellan while retaining time in Buenos Aires and Santiago. If your priority is **hiking around El Chalten and Tierra del Fuego**, compare the [13-day Argentina–Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/), which visits Ushuaia, Laguna Capri and Laguna de los Tres.

Another option is [Argentina and Brazil with a beach stay](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/), where the route continues from Perito Moreno to Iguazu and the ocean. All multi-country tours can be found in the [route catalog](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about the VIP Patagonia tour

### Are all excursions private?

Most included excursions are private, but **the boat trip to the Strait of Magellan islands is an exception**. Every voyage follows its own operating schedule.

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide?

A Russian-speaking guide is provided in Buenos Aires and Santiago, and an interpreter in El Calafate. Excursions in Puerto Natales and Punta Arenas are conducted by an English-speaking guide.

### Are flights included in the price from $8520?

No. Both international and domestic flights are listed among the expenses charged separately.

### Can multi-day trekking be added?

The published ten-day itinerary focuses on sightseeing visits to national parks. Athletic trekking would require a separate program and a review of the logistics.

## Maya World in 10 days: exploring Guatemala and Honduras

Maya history and culture are at the heart of this journey. Over **10 days and 9 nights**, guests visit [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), the [Lake Atitlan](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/) area, the highland Chichicastenango market, ancient Iximche, [Copan](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/), [Quirigua](/guatemala/place/quirigua/) and [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/).

This journey connects **Guatemala and Honduras**. It reveals the Maya not as a single vanished civilization but through historic cities, stone monuments, writing and the region's living communities. The days first introduce travelers to the contemporary cultural context and then move through the archaeological centers.

## What each archaeological stop offers

| Site | Main focus of the visit |
| --- | --- |
| Iximche | History of the highland Kaqchikel Maya |
| Copan | Temples, carved stelae and hieroglyphs |
| Quirigua | Monumental stelae and inscriptions |
| Tikal | A large ancient city in the tropical forest |

These are four different stops. Seen together, they show that Maya architecture, political centers and artistic traditions in Guatemala and Honduras cannot be reduced to one kind of pyramid.

## Antigua and Atitlan: the Maya today and after the conquest

The route begins in Guatemala City, followed by a transfer to [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/). Here visitors explore colonial architecture, then travel to San Antonio Aguas Calientes and Santiago Zamora. The following day includes [Iximche](/guatemala/place/iximche/) and the drive to [Lake Atitlan](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/).

Iximche is associated with Kaqchikel Maya history immediately before and during the Spanish conquest. This differs from the earlier Classic-period cities of Copan and Tikal. The sequence helps travelers see how the region's history continued well beyond the height of its great stone-built centers.

At Lake Atitlan, the program includes San Juan La Laguna and [Santiago Atitlan](/guatemala/place/santiago-atitlan/). Encounters with local communities, crafts and everyday traditions, including weaving, bring the culture to life. These visits connect archaeological discoveries with living traditions in Guatemala today.

## Chichicastenango: fit the travel dates to the market

Day five is devoted to [Chichicastenango](/guatemala/place/chichicastenango/) market and the return to Guatemala City. A specific scheduling rule applies: **the market visit is only on Thursday or Sunday**.

This matters on a ten-day journey. Selecting arrival dates without considering market day may require a different sequence of days and changes to the time allocated for nearby sites. It makes sense to check the suitable weekday first, before choosing flights.

## Copan and Quirigua: why the two Maya centers matter

Day six includes the National Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology in Guatemala City, followed by travel to Honduras. Day seven is fully dedicated to [Copan](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/), known for its stone carving and hieroglyphic texts. This UNESCO World Heritage site helps explain the artistic and political traditions of the southeastern Maya world.

On day eight, the route returns to Guatemala via [Quirigua](/guatemala/place/quirigua/), particularly celebrated for its large carved stelae depicting rulers and recording historical events. Quirigua is also UNESCO-listed. Comparing the two centers shows how related cultural traditions took different forms in monumental art.

Crossing from Guatemala to Honduras and back requires checking documents and entry rules for each traveler's nationality. Permission to enter one country does not automatically satisfy the other country's requirements.

## Tikal: an ancient city in the forests of Peten

Day nine is devoted to [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) in the Peten region. Unlike the highland stops, this archaeological site is surrounded by humid tropical forest. UNESCO recognizes both the archaeological and natural importance of the national park.

Allow time to walk between structures and plazas, and prepare for humidity, sun exposure and insects. Sightings of particular wild animals cannot be promised; the main attraction is the ancient city and its architecture.

After the excursion, a **domestic Flores – Guatemala City flight** is included in the program. Day ten is reserved for departure.

## Included services and who this tour suits

The package includes a Russian-speaking guide, transfers, accommodation at the listed hotels, scheduled excursions, some meals according to the daily itinerary, accommodation taxes and the Flores – Guatemala City flight. Extra activities, airport fees and personal expenses are separate.

Maya World particularly suits travelers interested in **archaeology, inscriptions on stone stelae, historic capitals and the living cultures of local communities**. To add a volcano, Semuc Champey, caves and the Caribbean coast, compare the [14-day Best of Guatemala itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-guatemala/). It is longer and includes a substantially larger nature-focused section.

## Frequently asked questions about Maya World

### Why does the route include Honduras?

Because a full day is dedicated to Copan, one of the major Maya archaeological centers. The route then returns to Guatemala via Quirigua.

### Are all attractions from the same historical period?

No. Iximche reflects later highland Maya history, while Copan, Quirigua and Tikal primarily showcase the monumental heritage of the Classic period.

### Can we visit Chichicastenango Market on any day?

No. Under the agreed itinerary, the market is visited on a Thursday or Sunday. It is best to choose the trip's start date with this condition in mind.

### Is the return flight from the Tikal region included?

Yes. The **domestic Flores – Guatemala City flight** is included. International flights are arranged separately.

## Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua in 13 days: the nature and cities of Central America

This itinerary combines **3 countries in 13 days**: Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua. First, discover [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) and the Panama Canal, then travel to the mountain and coastal regions of Panama. Costa Rica offers national parks, cloud forests and volcanic scenery. The final part takes place in colonial [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/) and around Masaya Volcano.

The journey is especially appealing to travelers who want to see the region's different natural environments and cultures without having to organize dozens of transfers. It is an active route, however: almost every day involves an excursion or a transfer, leaving less free time than a stay in a single resort town.

## How the three stages differ

| Country | Highlights |
|---|---|
| Panama | Canal, Chagres, Baru, Chiriqui |
| Costa Rica | Manuel Antonio, Monteverde, Arenal |
| Nicaragua | Granada, Managua, Masaya Volcano |

The first part in Panama focuses on history and engineering. At Miraflores, visitors can see the Panama Canal locks, while the capital's older neighborhoods retain traces of its colonial past. It introduces a city on a major shipping route between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

An excursion to [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) follows, including a river trip and a visit to an Embera village. This cultural visit is an encounter with a living community, not a museum display. The program introduces local customs and crafts; visitors should ask permission before taking photographs of people.

## Panama: from Baru Volcano to Pacific islands

Beyond the capital, the route heads into the highlands of Chiriqui. One stop is [Baru Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/). Highland weather can differ sharply from the heat of Panama City; warm clothes are needed for the ascent and exposure to mountain winds. Views of two oceans are possible only when visibility is good and cannot be promised in all weather.

Another part of this stage covers [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and the Chiriqui Gulf National Marine Park. Coastal scenery and island excursions come to the fore. The precise program for the day depends on sea conditions and the chosen boat route.

**The domestic Panama City – David flight is included in the tour.** This is an important detail: the flight connects the capital to the west of the country, although onward road trips and transfers still take time.

## Costa Rica: national parks and wildlife watching

The Costa Rican stage starts around [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) on the Pacific coast. Its national park combines tropical forest and beaches. Monkeys and sloths may be seen on walks, but wildlife sightings depend on animal behavior and are not guaranteed. Park entry regulations and rules restricting contact with wildlife apply.

The route continues via the Tarcoles River to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), a cloud-forest area where trees carry mosses and epiphytes. Weather can change during a single excursion. Closed-toe shoes and a light waterproof jacket are useful for walking here.

The next stop is the [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) area. The route includes a boat crossing on Lake Arenal, then continues to [Cano Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/). Its wetlands are especially rewarding for birdwatching. Some routes can be affected by rainy-season conditions, making the season and current water levels relevant.

## Nicaragua: colonial Granada and Masaya Volcano

On day eleven, the trip crosses from Costa Rica into Nicaragua and arrives in Granada, with its historic squares and colonial buildings. The next day includes a visit to Managua and the Masaya area.

[Masaya Volcano National Park](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) is an active volcanic zone. Access to the crater and individual areas depends on park management and volcanic activity. If a section is temporarily closed, a visit to the crater edge cannot be guaranteed; access follows current safety regulations.

At the end of the journey, you travel across Lake Nicaragua toward Zapango Island, experiencing the local natural landscape after the city and volcano visits.

## What the $8 624 price includes

The journey costs **from $8 624**. The price includes hotel accommodation, a Russian-speaking guide, transfers, excursions, accommodation taxes and the domestic Panama City – David flight. Meals are specified by day: breakfast, lunch or dinner where included.

**Additional activities, airport fees and personal expenses are paid separately.** For other tickets and cross-border travel, the precise transfer and flight arrangements matter. The inclusion of one domestic flight should not be taken to mean that all air travel is covered.

## Preparing for several borders and different weather

Travel takes you between Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua. Each border crossing requires a valid passport, attention to entry requirements, proof of onward travel and permitted length of stay according to citizenship. Check exact rules before traveling, and allow time for formalities on transport days.

Light clothing, rain and sun protection are useful in the lowland tropics, while Baru and Monteverde call for warmer layers. Comfortable closed-toe shoes are important on wet forest paths. The tour suits those who enjoy active excursions and are comfortable with frequent changes of hotels, weather and means of transport.

## Frequently asked questions about three Central American countries

### Which countries are on the main route?

Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua. The journey moves from east to west and concludes its exploration of the region in Nicaragua.

### Is the domestic flight within Panama included?

Yes. **Panama City – David** is listed among included services. Other flights need to be considered separately according to the trip arrangements.

### Are wildlife sightings guaranteed in Manuel Antonio and Cano Negro?

No. Excursions visit natural habitats, but sightings of specific species depend on season, weather and animal behavior.

### Can Masaya Volcano's summit be visited regardless of activity?

No. Access to an active volcano's attractions depends on restrictions imposed by park authorities and current safety conditions.

## Panama and Costa Rica in 10 days: the canal, Embera culture and national parks

This **10-day, 9-night** tour combines the engineering history of the Panama Canal with Costa Rica's natural landscapes. It begins in [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) and [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/), including a meeting with the Embera people. The journey then continues in Costa Rica: [Poas Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/), La Paz Waterfalls, [Cano Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/).

This route suits travelers who enjoy **combining culture with nature and wildlife watching**, with Russian-speaking assistance and private transport. It is not a typical beach package: most days are devoted to reserves, cities and transfers.

## The first three nights: Panama City, the canal and the Embera community

The program includes **3 nights** in [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/). You take a sightseeing tour of historic and modern neighborhoods and visit the Panama Canal's Miraflores Locks, where the connection between sea transport, canal engineering and national development becomes apparent.

Another day is devoted to [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/). The program includes a trip along the river in a traditional dugout canoe and an introduction to Embera culture. This is a nature excursion with a cultural component. The route, weather and activities of local participants influence how the visit actually unfolds.

If Panama's sights are your main interest, see [other tours around Panama](/panama/tour/). This trip deliberately limits the Panama section to three nights so that there is time to explore Costa Rica.

## Costa Rica: from volcanoes to forest beside the ocean

The Costa Rican part starts with [Poas Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and [La Paz Waterfall Gardens](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/), including lunch. Access to volcanic attractions can depend on current restrictions and conditions in the protected area; actual visiting rules matter when choosing dates.

The next stop is the [La Fortuna and Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) area, followed by a boat trip on the Rio Frio in [Cano Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/). The excursion offers opportunities to watch wetland wildlife, but sightings of specific animals are never guaranteed.

In [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), the itinerary includes a walk on the Sky Monteverde suspension bridges and **a night tour in Kinkajou Park**. This differs greatly from a daytime walk near the coast: evening conditions and cloud-forest humidity call for closed-toe shoes and rain protection.

The final stage is in [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/), where a natural park adjoins Pacific beaches. The program leaves more time by the sea after the busy nature excursions.

## Overnight stays and transport: what is specified

Accommodation is divided between four hotels:

| Location | Nights |
|---|---:|
| Hilton Garden Inn Panama City | 3 |
| Los Lagos | 2 |
| Ficus | 1 |
| San Bada | 3 |

All listed hotel stays include breakfast. If necessary, the company can substitute accommodation of the same category under the program terms.

**A Russian-speaking guide accompanies the entire route**, with comfortable private transport. This distinguishes the tour from some other Central American programs where guiding depends on the specific excursion. Individual activities, including the boat outing and night walk, are still subject to the rules of their natural sites.

## What is included and what costs extra

Services include a Panama City tour, Chagres National Park, Poas Volcano and La Paz Waterfalls with lunch, a boat tour in Cano Negro with lunch, the night excursion, suspension bridges in Monteverde, the named hotels, a guide and transport along the route.

**Medical insurance is not included**, nor are international flights, extra meals, optional activities and tips. Account for these when calculating the full trip cost. A Russian-speaking guide does not automatically mean insurance coverage or guaranteed access to a national park in any weather.

The inclusion of a specific international flight between the countries is not separately confirmed. Before booking, clarify the border crossing, international air tickets and check-in arrangements against the current schedule.

## How this route differs from Guatemala and Costa Rica

On the [15-day Guatemala – Costa Rica tour](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-costa-rica/), the first half focuses on Antigua, Lake Atitlan, Chichicastenango Market and Tikal. It has more Maya archaeology and a different set of Costa Rican stops; in particular, its main program does not include Monteverde.

**Panama – Costa Rica in 10 days** is better suited to travelers who want the Panama Canal, Embera culture and specific nature excursions in Cano Negro, Monteverde and Manuel Antonio. For a trip focused on the nature of one country, see [Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Panama – Costa Rica

### Can we see the Panama Canal?

Yes. The Panama City tour includes the Miraflores Locks, while Chagres National Park offers a different view of Panama.

### Are excursions in Monteverde included?

Yes. The Sky Monteverde suspension bridges and a night tour in Kinkajou Park are included.

### Is medical insurance included?

No. Insurance is explicitly listed among services excluded from the price.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide?

Yes. Russian-speaking accompaniment and comfortable private transport are provided throughout the itinerary.
